applicable_when: The kernel is a layout transpose (NHWC to NCHW) + bias add. Input in_ptr0 has strides (290400, 1, 5280, 96), so the load index y0 + 96*x2 + 290400*y1 has stride 96 between consecutive x2 elements. With XBLOCK=128, each warp loads 128 floats spaced 96 floats apart — completely uncoalesced, saturating L2 at 97.15%. The output store x2 + 3025*y3 IS contiguous in x2 (stride-1), so stores are coalesced but the compiler does not know the alignment. Adding tl.multiple_of and tl.max_contiguous hints on the output index and the xindex range tells the compiler these accesses are 128-bit aligned and contiguous, enabling the backend to emit 128-bit (float4) vectorized store instructions. Additionally, switching to @triton.autotune allows exploration of tile configurations that better match the memory access pattern.
